chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from the one who told him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

he was asked about the meaning of 'In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful', so he said: The Ba is the brilliance of Allah, and the Sin is the splendor of Allah, and the Mim is the Kingdom of Allah. I asked: And Allah? He said: The Alif is the blessings of Allah upon His creation from the favor of our Guardianship, and the Lam is the obligation of Allah upon His creation of our Guardianship. I asked: And the Ha? He said: Abasement for those who oppose Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, may the prayers of Allah be upon them. I asked: And al-Rahman? He said: For the entire world. I asked: And al-Rahim? He said: Specifically for the Believers.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of the letters in Bismillah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this unique hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a theological exegesis of the letters in 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim', linking each to divine attributes and the concept of Wilayah. He explains that the letters represent Allah's brilliance, splendor, and kingdom, with the Alif signifying blessings through the Imams' authority, and the Ha signifying the abasement of their opponents. This interpretation underscores the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in understanding divine mercy and sovereignty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and political leadership of the Imams as the manifestation of God's grace.
